commands_used: answer 1. I am a hunter freed from the Owing at Ashgate Landing by Vosh-Leera, root-herald of Jal-Veesa. She secretly serves the Toh-Reel-Ka, Secret Warriors of the Xeech-Leel, who try to prevent another Umbriel-type disaster and use friendless strangers as spies. Jal-Veesa Hist is dying and trees along the river are sickening; nobody knows why. 2. Go to Vosh-Leera (marker) at her House in Jal-Veesa and ask for her second task. 3. I can accept the task she gives, or ask questions first; I have 50 gold and two lockpicks. I mean to pursue the truth. I do not yet know what the task is. 4. I do not understand why the trees are sick, what the second task is, or the full nature of the Toh-Reel-Ka. I could ask Vosh-Leera, and Weeltul about the sap, scar and Umbriel.

answer 1. Vosh-Leera gave me a cup of Hist sap drawn before the scar closed. The trees are joined at the root, so drinking it lets me ask where the sickness is and see what the trees show. 2. Drink the cup in front of Vosh-Leera, here in Jal-Veesa, then tell her everything I see. 3. I can drink it now as asked, or first talk to her/Weeltul about the risks; I mean to report truthfully what I see. 4. I do not know what drinking the sap will do to me or whether it is safe. I could ask Vosh-Leera or Weeltul.

answer 1. I drank the sap and saw a vision: a young Hist among stilt huts beside a woven weir, and a reed hide beside a lone dead tree. This is where the trees show the sickness is. 2. Tell Vosh-Leera what I saw, here in Jal-Veesa. 3. I can tell her everything truthfully (my aim), or hold back; I mean to tell the truth. 4. I do not know which place the weir and stilt huts are (perhaps Reed-Sill Weir?), who or what the reed hide and dead tree belong to, or what causes the sickness. Vosh-Leera or Weeltul may know.

answer 1. The vision showed Teel-Fen Weir, a Sedge-Wardens camp south of Jal-Veesa down the creek, where a young Hist grew from Jal-Veesa tree roots. A reed hide with jars of sap sits west of the weir by a lone dead tree; someone may be keeping sap. Vosh-Leera told me to be careful at the hide. 2. Go to Teel-Fen Weir and speak to Heem-Jasa, the tree-minder, on the platform round the tree. 3. I can go straight to Heem-Jasa and ask what she knows, or look at the hide; Vosh-Leera advised seeing Heem-Jasa first. I mean to find the truth. 4. I do not know who is keeping the jars, why the lone tree is dead, or what causes the sickness. Heem-Jasa may know.

answer 1. Heem-Jasa says her young tree was drained and its scar sealed with grey paste three nights ago, not by her people. Three strangers (Unbound Sap-Takers) keep jars at the reed hide west of the weir; they seem to be draining Hist trees, which may explain the sickness. 2. Take the Note to the Sap-Takers from the reed hide west of Teel-Fen Weir. 3. I can fight the three, shoot them from the reeds east of the hide, or creep to the hide open west side unseen to take the note and jars. I mean to find the truth, so the note matters most. 4. I do not know who the Unbound Sap-Takers work for, what the grey paste is, or why they take sap. The note may tell me.

answer 1. I took the note without a fight. It shows the Sap-Takers crew is ordered by their master to bring jars of sap to Karsh-Naal Camp and seal every scar behind them. So someone organized is draining Hist trees, which likely causes the sickness. 2. Return to Heem-Jasa at Teel-Fen Weir and be straight with her; she will ask whether her tree will live. 3. I can tell her the truth, including what the note says, or soften it; I mean to tell the truth. Later I can go to Karsh-Naal Camp. 4. I do not know who the master is, where Karsh-Naal Camp is, or why they want the sap. I could ask Heem-Jasa and Vosh-Leera.

answer 1. The sickness comes from someone draining Hist trees of sap and sealing the scars with grey paste. The Sap-Takers crew sends jars to Karsh-Naal Camp. I told Heem-Jasa the truth and she will teach and sell to me. 2. The quest is complete; the next lead is Karsh-Naal Camp, and reporting to Vosh-Leera. 3. I can go to Karsh-Naal Camp, report to Vosh-Leera, or learn alchemy from Heem-Jasa. 4. I do not know where Karsh-Naal Camp is, who the master is, or why they want the sap. Heem-Jasa has a topic on the camp.

answer Notes: I work (unknowingly at first) for Vosh-Leera of Jal-Veesa, who serves the Toh-Reel-Ka. I drank Hist sap and saw Teel-Fen Weir, south of Jal-Veesa. Heem-Jasa, minder of its young Hist, showed me the scar sealed with grey paste three nights ago. Strangers (Unbound Sap-Takers, three) work from a reed hide west of the weir. I took the Note to the Sap-Takers without a fight: their master orders them to bring jars to Karsh-Naal Camp and seal every scar. So trees are being drained and sealed, which is probably why they sicken. I told Heem-Jasa the truth that her tree may die, so she will teach me alchemy and sell sap, swamp fungus and eggshells. I carry 50 gold, two lockpicks and the note. Unknown: who the master is, where Karsh-Naal Camp is, why they want sap. Next: ask Heem-Jasa about Karsh-Naal Camp and Umbriel, report to Vosh-Leera, then go to the camp.
